item.title: QVS edge MGM 17-15 to secure U16 Super Deans final against Grammar
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 15/08/2026 Queen Victoria School had to dig deep to secure their place in the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union U16 final, defeating MGM High School 17-15 at Buckhurst Ground.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 15/08/2026

Queen Victoria School had to dig deep to secure their place in the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union U16 final, defeating MGM High School 17-15 at Buckhurst Ground.

The match gave fans what they came for, as both teams showcased some superb rugby.

The match came down to the wire, but costly mistakes denied MGM the win.

QVS slotted a penalty with just a few seconds remaining to secure the victory over MGM.

Meanwhile, Suva Grammar School booked their place in the U16 final after dominating Nasinu Secondary School 22-0.

In other results, QVS defeated MGM High School 22-15, while Ratu Navula College edged RKS 26-25 in the U14 semi-finals. RKS came from behind to edge rivals Queen Victoria School 28-26, while Marist Brothers High School defeated Lelean Memorial School 16-3 in the U15 semi-finals.

The U18 semi-finals will see Suva Grammar School take on Ra High School at 3pm at Churchill Park, while Lelean Memorial School will meet Nasinu Secondary School at 3.40pm at HFC Bank Stadium.

Hughes says they know the task ahead will not be easy as Lae City are a good team, but Rewa will stick to their game plan and work hard to get the result they need.
item.content:encoded:
Rewa FC captain Setareki Hughes says the side knows it is a do-or-die match when they face Papua New Guinea’s Lae City FC for a place in the OFC Men’s Champions League semi-finals this afternoon .

Hughes says they know the task ahead will not be easy as Lae City are a good team, but Rewa will stick to their game plan and work hard to get the result they need.

He says the key will be staying composed throughout the match as they know the win will not come easily.

Hughes says the players are determined to make their supporters proud and will give everything to secure a place in the semi-finals.

Rewa FC will face Lae City FC at 3pm this afternoon at 4R Stadium, Govind Park in Ba.

Nasinu no stranger to Super Deans semi-final pressure
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 14/08/2026 Playing in the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans semi-finals is nothing new for Nasinu Secondary School, as they were the runners-up in last year’s Under-18 grade, losing to Ratu Kadavulevu School 53-15 in the final.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 14/08/2026

Playing in the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans semi-finals is nothing new for Nasinu Secondary School, as they were the runners-up in last year’s Under-18 grade, losing to Ratu Kadavulevu School 53-15 in the final.

Nasinu will field three teams in tomorrow's semi-finals with the school’s Under-18 side set to take on Eastern Zone champions Lelean Memorial School.

They will also feature in the Deans Under-16 grade, where they will meet Suva Grammar School at 10.45am at the HFC Bank Stadium, while their Raluve Under-16 side will face Adi Cakobau School at 9am at Buckhurst Park.

Meanwhile, the Lelean Under-18 side is the only undefeated team heading into the national semi-finals.

Lelean will face Nasinu at 3.40pm tomorrow at the HFC Bank Stadium, while Ra High School will take on Grammar at 3pm at Churchill Park.
